checklist.step: Refresh the curriculum from the last year's actual failures
actions: Pull the year's breach root causes, DSAR failures and notice exceptions from the GRC platform and list the top ten human failure modes - misdirected post, wrong claimant emailed, medical report attached to the wrong file, data exported to a personal drive, request not recognised as a DSAR.
Write or rewrite a scenario for each failure mode using a real, anonymised case so the module teaches this company's mistakes rather than generic principles.

Add the 72-hour breach reporting message explicitly: report any suspected personal data breach within one hour through the single internal route, because the controller's 72-hour clock starts on awareness.
Take the Data Protection Officer's approval on the content before it is built.
checklist.done: the curriculum carries a scenario for each of the year's top failure modes and a DPO-approved content sign-off.

checklist.step: Build the role-based training matrix
actions: Map every job profile in the HRIS to a training tier: all-staff foundation; enhanced for anyone touching health, medical or conviction data; specialist for SIU, marketing, HR, and developers and data scientists with production data access.
Define per tier the module set, the pass mark and the frequency - foundation annual, enhanced annual plus a half-year refresher.
Cross-check the enhanced tier against the Art. 30 register's special-category entries so no team processing medical evidence sits on the foundation tier.
Publish the matrix and have each function head confirm their population's tier assignment in writing.
checklist.done: every job profile has a tier, the enhanced tier reconciles to the register's special-category activities, and function heads have confirmed in writing.

checklist.step: Build the modules and their assessments
actions: Author each module in the LMS with a version number and an effective date, and retire the prior version on the same day.
Build a scored assessment with a minimum of 12 scenario-based questions per module and an 80% pass mark, with two re-sits permitted before manager escalation.
Include a question set on breach recognition and the one-hour internal reporting expectation, and one on recognising a data-subject request arriving by phone or in a complaint.
Run an accessibility and translation pass so every covered market receives the module in its working language.
checklist.done: each module is versioned in the LMS with an 80% scored assessment, breach and DSAR recognition questions, and market translations.

checklist.step: Drive assignment off the HRIS worker feed
actions: Configure the nightly worker feed from the HRIS to the LMS to carry job profile, org unit, country, worker type and start date for employees and contractors alike.
Write the assignment rules so the tier follows the job profile and org unit, and so a transfer re-assigns the new tier automatically.
Include contingent workers, contractors and long-term temporary staff - their omission is the most common coverage gap.
Run a reconciliation each week between HRIS headcount and LMS assigned population and investigate any difference above 1%.
checklist.done: assignment is automated from the HRIS feed for all worker types, and the weekly headcount reconciliation runs within 1%.

checklist.step: Launch the annual campaign on 1 March
actions: Open the campaign on 1 March with a 30 April close and assign the current module version to the whole in-scope population.
Send the launch communication from the Data Protection Officer, naming the deadline and the consequence of non-completion.
Schedule reminders at two weeks and one week before close, and switch to weekly line-manager escalation lists after close.
Publish a live completion dashboard by function so leaders can see their own gap without asking.
checklist.done: the campaign is open with the current version assigned, dated reminders scheduled and a live completion dashboard published.

checklist.step: Train new joiners inside 30 days of start
actions: Trigger assignment on the joiner's start date from the HRIS event, not from a manual onboarding checklist.
Set the due date at start date plus 30 days with LMS reminders at day 14, 21 and 27.
Escalate at day 28 to the line manager and at day 31 to the function head, and record every escalation.
Apply the same rule to internal transfers into an enhanced or specialist tier, since the receiving role carries the obligation.
checklist.done: every joiner and in-scope transfer has an event-triggered assignment with a 30-day due date and a logged escalation path.

checklist.step: Deliver the specialist modules where the risk sits
actions: Run live sessions for claims handlers and medical underwriters on handling medical evidence - who may see it, how it is stored, what goes in the file note and what does not.
Run a session for SIU investigators on Art. 10 conviction data, the lawful basis for anti-fraud database checks and the limits on covert activity.
Run a session for developers and data scientists on production-data access, pseudonymisation, and the prohibition on copying production personal data into test environments.
Record attendance against the LMS record so live delivery is evidenced the same way as e-learning.
checklist.done: each specialist population has a delivered session with attendance recorded against the LMS record.

checklist.step: Train the front line to recognise breaches and rights requests
actions: Deliver a short module and a desk aid on recognising a data-subject request in any wording - 'send me everything you hold', 'delete me', 'stop writing to me' - and the route to raise it the same day.
Drill the one-hour breach reporting rule with worked examples: a letter sent to the wrong claimant, a call recording emailed externally, an adjuster's laptop left in a car.
Add the recognition checks to the quality-monitoring scorecard so the behaviour is measured on live calls, not just tested once.
Feed misses found in quality monitoring back into the next coaching cycle with the agent named to their supervisor.
checklist.done: front-line staff have the desk aid, the drill is delivered, and recognition is scored in quality monitoring with coaching feedback.

checklist.step: Chase non-completion up an escalation ladder
actions: Publish the overdue list daily after campaign close, by individual, line manager and function.
Escalate at 7 days overdue to the line manager, at 14 days to the function head, and at 21 days to the executive sponsor with the names attached.
For anyone with special-category data access still overdue at 21 days, ask the Access Management Analyst to suspend the relevant entitlement until completion.
Record every escalation and every access suspension so the enforcement is provable.
checklist.done: the ladder runs on schedule with recorded escalations and access suspension applied to overdue special-category-access staff.

checklist.step: Trigger targeted retraining after incidents and failures
actions: Take the post-incident review output and identify the team and behaviour involved, not just the individual.
Assign a targeted module or coaching session to that team with a 30-day completion date from the review date.
Do the same after a DSAR SLA breach or a notice exception traced to a team's process.
Record the trigger, the population, the due date and the completion so the corrective action is evidenced rather than asserted.
checklist.done: each incident or failure with a human root cause has an assigned targeted module for the team, due within 30 days, with completion recorded.

checklist.step: Capture confidentiality and instruction commitments
actions: Confirm every employee and contractor contract carries the confidentiality undertaking Art. 28(3)(b) and Art. 32(4) rely on, and that contractors' agencies flow it down.
Take an annual acceptable-use and data-handling attestation alongside the training completion, recording that staff will process personal data only on the controller's instruction per Art. 29.
Store the attestation with the training record so completion and commitment are produced together.
Chase non-attestation on the same escalation ladder as non-completion.
checklist.done: every worker has a current confidentiality commitment and a dated Art. 29 attestation filed with the training record.

checklist.step: Report training coverage to the Privacy Committee
actions: Publish completion by function and tier, average assessment score, re-sit rate, new-joiner 30-day compliance and outstanding names by function.
Show the special-category-access population separately, since the threshold there is 100% rather than 98%.
Trend assessment scores by question topic so weak content - usually breach recognition - is visible and can be rewritten.
Table the pack quarterly with the actions agreed against each function below threshold.
checklist.done: a quarterly pack shows completion by function and tier, score trends and named outstanding staff, with committee-agreed actions minuted.

checklist.step: Retain and version the training evidence
actions: Export at campaign close the per-person completion record with course version, completion date and assessment score, and lock it as the year's evidence file.
Archive the module content itself at its version so what was taught in a given year can be produced, not just who completed it.
Apply the 6-years-after-leaving retention label to person-level records and confirm leaver records are not purged with the HRIS record.
Confirm the file is searchable by person, function, course version and completion date.
checklist.done: a locked annual evidence file with per-person records and archived module content is retained and searchable.

checklist.step: Test the curriculum against the year's regulatory changes
actions: Review the module text against any EDPB guideline, ICO guidance or supervisory-authority decision issued in the year that changes practice.
Check the module states the correct deadlines - the 72-hour authority notification, the one-month DSAR response, the 30-day Art. 14 notice window - since stale numbers teach non-compliance.
Confirm the module names the Irish DPC and the ICO correctly as the complaint routes and the DPO as the internal contact point.
Sign the content review and date it before the campaign opens.
checklist.done: the module is reviewed against the year's guidance with all statutory deadlines verified and a dated counsel sign-off before launch.

checklist.step: Log training exceptions and take DPO sign-off
actions: Raise an exception for each function below the completion threshold at close, each new joiner past 30 days, each in-scope population with no assigned module and each targeted retraining not completed.
Assign root cause - worker type excluded from the feed, job profile unmapped, contractor population outside HRIS, manager not escalating - and a named owner.
Decide whether access is suspended for individuals still outstanding and record who took the decision.
Sign the annual completion conclusion only when the outstanding population is either complete or access-suspended.
checklist.done: every training exception has an issue with root cause, owner, an access decision and a DPO-signed annual completion conclusion.

testing.step: Build the in-scope workforce population
actions: Extract all active workers at campaign close with worker id, job profile, org unit, country, worker type and start date, for EU and UK entities.
Add contingent workers, agency staff and long-term contractors from the vendor and access-management sources, since these are routinely absent from the HRIS extract.
Add leavers who were active during the campaign window, so departure cannot be used to explain non-completion.
Sign the population as complete and record the sources, run date and headcount.
testing.done: a signed workforce population covers employees, contingent workers and in-window leavers with headcount recorded.

testing.step: Reconcile the workforce population to LMS assignments
actions: Extract every assignment and completion record for the campaign with worker id, module, version, due date, completion date and assessment score.
Match both ways: workers with no assignment, and assignments with no matching active worker.
Compute the coverage gap by worker type and org unit and identify which populations the assignment rules missed.
Treat any in-scope worker with no assignment as an automatic fail, ahead of any completion analysis.
testing.done: the two-way match is complete, the coverage gap is quantified by worker type and org unit, and unassigned workers are listed as fails.

testing.step: Test the role matrix against actual data access
actions: Pull the entitlement report for the systems holding health, medical and conviction data - the claims platform, the underwriting workstation, the medical evidence store and the fraud system.
Match every holder of those entitlements to their assigned training tier and list anyone on the foundation tier who holds special-category access.
Cross-check the enhanced tier population against the Art. 30 register's special-category activities and their named teams.
Treat a mis-tiered special-category-access population as a matrix defect, not an individual defect.
testing.done: every special-category entitlement holder is confirmed on the enhanced or specialist tier, or the mis-tiering is logged as a matrix defect.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of the special-category-access population, since the threshold there is 100% completion.
Take 100% of joiners in the period and 100% of individuals named in incident root causes requiring targeted retraining.
Take 40 further workers at random with a recorded seed, stratified across function, country and worker type.
Record population size, seed, strata and draw date so the sample is reproducible.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all special-category-access staff, joiners, retraining subjects and a stratified random tail.

testing.step: Recompute the completion and deadline maths
actions: Recompute the completion rate by function and tier from the raw extract rather than reading the dashboard figure, and compare to the 98% and 100% thresholds.
For joiners, recompute elapsed days = completion date minus start date and list every completion past 30 days with its overrun.
For targeted retraining, recompute elapsed days from the post-incident review date and list every completion past 30 days.
Check that completions dated after the campaign close were counted as late rather than folded into the headline rate.
testing.done: completion rates and every 30-day window are recomputed from raw data, with late completions listed and headline-rate manipulation tested.

testing.step: Verify completion records are genuine, not clicked through
actions: For 25 sampled records, read the time-in-module and compare it to the module's designed duration; flag completions materially shorter than the content allows.
Read the assessment score and the number of attempts, and list anyone passed after more than the permitted two re-sits.
Confirm the version completed is the current year's version and not a prior-year record carried forward.
For live sessions, trace the LMS record to the signed attendance sheet or the meeting attendance export.
testing.done: each sampled completion is corroborated by plausible duration, permitted attempts, the current version and, for live sessions, attendance evidence.

testing.step: Re-read the module content against the obligations it teaches
actions: Take the version completed this year and check it states the 72-hour supervisory-authority window, the one-month DSAR response, the 30-day Art. 14 notice window and the one-hour internal breach reporting expectation.
Confirm it names the DPO as the contact point and the Irish DPC and the ICO as the complaint routes.
Confirm the enhanced module covers Art. 9 special-category handling and the specialist module covers Art. 10 conviction data for SIU.
List every stale or wrong statement as a content defect with the slide or question reference.
testing.done: the completed module version is read against every deadline and contact it teaches, with stale statements listed by slide reference.

testing.step: Test whether training changed behaviour where it was targeted
actions: Take the failure modes the curriculum targeted and count the incidents of that type before and after the campaign.
For teams that received targeted retraining, compare their incident and DSAR-recognition failure counts in the 90 days before and after.
Pull contact-centre quality-monitoring scores for DSAR and breach recognition and trend them across the campaign date.
Record where the numbers did not move and hand that to the Privacy Officer as a content-effectiveness finding rather than a completion finding.
testing.done: before-and-after failure counts are computed for each targeted behaviour and unchanged metrics are raised as content-effectiveness findings.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the population or individual, the failure (no assignment, mis-tiered, non-completion, joiner past 30 days, excessive re-sits, stale content) and the function affected.
Assign root cause - worker type excluded from the feed, job profile unmapped, contractor outside HRIS, manager not escalating, content not refreshed - and a named owner.
Set a remediation date and, for outstanding special-category-access staff, confirm the access suspension decision was taken and applied.
Carry every open issue into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with root cause, owner, remediation date, an access decision where relevant, and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the overall completion rate, the special-category population completion rate, the new-joiner 30-day rate, the assignment-coverage rate and the content-defect count against the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the workpaper reference behind each figure.
Have the Internal Auditor, who sits outside Learning & Development and the Privacy Office and authored no sampled module, sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
Report to the Data Protection Officer, the Chief HR Officer and the Privacy Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper under REG-020-C07 in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, the five computed rates and a dated committee reporting entry is filed in the evidence repository.
